title: Settled Card Swipes to Customer Account Profiles
section: Section 8: Relational Joins & Financial Data Modeling
scenario: Connecting daily settled card swipes to customer account profiles on common key account_id to prepare audit reports.
businessObjective: Perform an exact INNER JOIN between CardSwipes and CustomerAccounts on account_id to project matched operational records.
schemaSnippet: `CardSwipes (record_id VARCHAR(32) PRIMARY KEY, account_id VARCHAR(32), amount_usd DECIMAL(12,2), created_at DATE)` & `CustomerAccounts (account_id VARCHAR(32) PRIMARY KEY, entity_name VARCHAR(64), status VARCHAR(20))`
targetQuery:
SELECT a.record_id, a.account_id, b.entity_name, a.amount_usd, a.created_at
FROM CardSwipes a
INNER JOIN CustomerAccounts b
  ON a.account_id = b.account_id
WHERE b.status = 'ACTIVE'
ORDER BY a.created_at DESC;
eli5Story: Think of linking sales receipts (CardSwipes) with the official customer list (CustomerAccounts). Only receipts that match an active customer on file make it to the report.
commonMistakes: Omitting the ON predicate or forgetting that records with unmatched account_id are dropped entirely from an INNER JOIN.
learningOutcomes: Master foreign key intersection matching and basic predicate filtering after joining.

title: Fintech Compound Revenue & Margin Reconciliation Suite #1
section: Section 8: Relational Joins & Financial Data Modeling
scenario: Aggregating gross revenue, COGS, and net gross margin per cost category by joining operational line items to product cost masters.
businessObjective: Join line item charges with unit cost masters, aggregate total volume and net margins grouped by reporting category, and filter with HAVING.
schemaSnippet: `Transactions_Fintech (tx_id VARCHAR(32) PRIMARY KEY, category_id VARCHAR(32), item_units INT, revenue_usd DECIMAL(12,2))` & `CostMaster_Fintech (category_id VARCHAR(32) PRIMARY KEY, category_name VARCHAR(64), unit_cost DECIMAL(10,2))`
targetQuery:
SELECT b.category_name,
       SUM(a.item_units) AS total_units_sold,
       SUM(a.revenue_usd) AS gross_revenue_usd,
       ROUND(SUM(a.item_units * b.unit_cost), 2) AS total_cogs_usd,
       ROUND(SUM(a.revenue_usd) - SUM(a.item_units * b.unit_cost), 2) AS gross_profit_usd
FROM Transactions_Fintech a
INNER JOIN CostMaster_Fintech b
  ON a.category_id = b.category_id
GROUP BY b.category_name
HAVING SUM(a.revenue_usd) > 50000.00
ORDER BY gross_profit_usd DESC;
eli5Story: You have sales records on one sheet and product manufacturing costs on another. You join them together, multiply units by cost to get COGS, subtract from revenue to get gross profit, and group by category.
commonMistakes: Performing arithmetic after aggregation without wrapping individual column metrics in SUM(); forgetting to group by all non-aggregated SELECT columns.
learningOutcomes: Combine INNER JOIN with multi-column aggregations, derived gross profit calculations, and HAVING filters.

schemaSnippet: `Transactions_Hardware (tx_id VARCHAR(32) PRIMARY KEY, category_id VARCHAR(32), item_units INT, revenue_usd DECIMAL(12,2))` & `CostMaster_Hardware (category_id VARCHAR(32) PRIMARY KEY, category_name VARCHAR(64), unit_cost DECIMAL(10,2))`
targetQuery:
SELECT b.category_name,
       SUM(a.item_units) AS total_units_sold,
       SUM(a.revenue_usd) AS gross_revenue_usd,
       ROUND(SUM(a.item_units * b.unit_cost), 2) AS total_cogs_usd,
       ROUND(SUM(a.revenue_usd) - SUM(a.item_units * b.unit_cost), 2) AS gross_profit_usd
FROM Transactions_Hardware a
INNER JOIN CostMaster_Hardware b

ORDER BY gross_profit_usd DESC;

title: Fintech Tri-Table Enterprise Audit & SLA Slippage Schedule #1
section: Section 8: Relational Joins & Financial Data Modeling
scenario: Joining dispatches across carrier contracts and delivery checkpoints to measure SLA breach rates and basis points cost penalties.
businessObjective: Perform a 3-table INNER JOIN linking dispatches to carrier service terms and audit checkpoints to calculate penalty adjustments.
schemaSnippet: `Dispatches_Fintech (dispatch_id VARCHAR(32) PRIMARY KEY, carrier_id VARCHAR(32), checkpoint_id VARCHAR(32), agreed_days INT, dispatch_date DATE)` & `Carriers_Fintech (carrier_id VARCHAR(32) PRIMARY KEY, carrier_name VARCHAR(64), penalty_rate_bps INT)` & `Checkpoints_Fintech (checkpoint_id VARCHAR(32) PRIMARY KEY, delivery_date DATE, delivery_status VARCHAR(20))`
targetQuery:
SELECT d.dispatch_id, c.carrier_name,
       d.agreed_days,
       DATEDIFF(k.delivery_date, d.dispatch_date) AS actual_transit_days,
       DATEDIFF(k.delivery_date, d.dispatch_date) - d.agreed_days AS days_delayed,
       CASE
         WHEN DATEDIFF(k.delivery_date, d.dispatch_date) > d.agreed_days THEN 'SLA_BREACH'
         ELSE 'ON_TIME'
       END AS compliance_status
FROM Dispatches_Fintech d
INNER JOIN Carriers_Fintech c
  ON d.carrier_id = c.carrier_id
INNER JOIN Checkpoints_Fintech k
  ON d.checkpoint_id = k.checkpoint_id
WHERE k.delivery_status = 'DELIVERED'
ORDER BY days_delayed DESC;
eli5Story: Connecting three sheets together: the dispatch manifest, the carrier rate contract, and the final delivery receipt. You calculate transit days, compare against agreed SLA, and flag breaches.
commonMistakes: Mixing up join conditions across 3 tables causing unintended Cartesian partial cross products; incorrect DATEDIFF argument ordering.
learningOutcomes: Master 3-table multi-join execution chaining and compound date math evaluation.

title: Fintech Driving Table Retention & Unassigned Master Check #1
section: Section 8: Relational Joins & Financial Data Modeling
scenario: Ensuring 100% of accounts appear on the executive roster even if they have zero associated billing transactions.
businessObjective: Use LEFT JOIN to retain all master accounts, displaying unassigned accounts cleanly.
schemaSnippet: `MasterAccounts_Fintech (account_id VARCHAR(32) PRIMARY KEY, account_name VARCHAR(64), tier VARCHAR(16))` & `ActivityLogs_Fintech (log_id VARCHAR(32) PRIMARY KEY, account_id VARCHAR(32), log_event VARCHAR(32))`
targetQuery:
SELECT m.account_id, m.account_name, m.tier, a.log_event
FROM MasterAccounts_Fintech m
LEFT JOIN ActivityLogs_Fintech a
  ON m.account_id = a.account_id
ORDER BY m.account_id ASC;
eli5Story: We start with the master customer directory and attach activity logs. If an account never did anything, they stay on the sheet with blank activity columns.
commonMistakes: Using an INNER JOIN by mistake which secretly drops newly onboarded or silent accounts.
learningOutcomes: Grasp left driving table preservation and NULL column padding.

title: Fintech Budget vs. Actual Spend Variance (COALESCE Zero-Preservation) #1
section: Section 8: Relational Joins & Financial Data Modeling
scenario: Calculating department budget variances where departments with $0 actual spend must remain visible with $0 rather than vanishing.
businessObjective: Join budget lines to actual expenses, applying COALESCE to actual spend to compute true variance.
schemaSnippet: `BudgetAllocations_Fintech (dept_id VARCHAR(32) PRIMARY KEY, dept_name VARCHAR(64), allocated_usd DECIMAL(12,2))` & `ActualSpend_Fintech (dept_id VARCHAR(32), actual_usd DECIMAL(12,2))`
targetQuery:
SELECT b.dept_id, b.dept_name,
       b.allocated_usd,
       COALESCE(SUM(s.actual_usd), 0.00) AS total_actual_spend,
       b.allocated_usd - COALESCE(SUM(s.actual_usd), 0.00) AS remaining_budget,
       CASE
         WHEN COALESCE(SUM(s.actual_usd), 0.00) > b.allocated_usd THEN 'OVER_BUDGET'
         WHEN COALESCE(SUM(s.actual_usd), 0.00) = 0.00 THEN 'ZERO_SPEND'
         ELSE 'WITHIN_BUDGET'
       END AS variance_audit_tag
FROM BudgetAllocations_Fintech b
LEFT JOIN ActualSpend_Fintech s
  ON b.dept_id = s.dept_id
GROUP BY b.dept_id, b.dept_name, b.allocated_usd
ORDER BY remaining_budget ASC;
eli5Story: If R&D was given $200k but spent $0, an INNER JOIN drops them entirely! A LEFT JOIN with COALESCE keeps R&D on the board and displays $0 spend and $200k remaining budget.
commonMistakes: Subtracting NULL directly from allocated budget: 'allocated - NULL' evaluates to NULL in SQL! You must wrap the right side in COALESCE(..., 0).
learningOutcomes: Master zero-preservation with COALESCE and conditional variance classification.

title: Fintech AR Aging & Pre-Aggregated Receipt Reconciliation #1
section: Section 8: Relational Joins & Financial Data Modeling
scenario: Reconciling multi-payment receipts against corporate invoices by pre-aggregating payments in a subquery to avoid duplicate invoice rows.
businessObjective: Left join invoices to an aggregated payment summary subquery to calculate outstanding balances and AR aging buckets.
schemaSnippet: `Invoices_Fintech (invoice_id VARCHAR(32) PRIMARY KEY, client_id VARCHAR(32), invoice_amt DECIMAL(12,2), due_date DATE)` & `Payments_Fintech (payment_id VARCHAR(32) PRIMARY KEY, invoice_id VARCHAR(32), amount_paid DECIMAL(12,2))`
targetQuery:
SELECT inv.invoice_id, inv.client_id, inv.invoice_amt,
       COALESCE(p.paid_sum, 0.00) AS total_paid_to_date,
       inv.invoice_amt - COALESCE(p.paid_sum, 0.00) AS current_balance_due,
       CASE
         WHEN inv.invoice_amt - COALESCE(p.paid_sum, 0.00) <= 0.00 THEN 'PAID_IN_FULL'
         WHEN DATEDIFF('2026-09-30', inv.due_date) > 90 THEN '90_PLUS_DAYS_OVERDUE'
         WHEN DATEDIFF('2026-09-30', inv.due_date) > 30 THEN '31_TO_90_DAYS_PAST_DUE'
         ELSE 'CURRENT'
       END AS ar_aging_tier
FROM Invoices_Fintech inv
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT invoice_id, SUM(amount_paid) AS paid_sum
  FROM Payments_Fintech
  GROUP BY invoice_id
) p ON inv.invoice_id = p.invoice_id
WHERE inv.invoice_amt - COALESCE(p.paid_sum, 0.00) > 0.00
ORDER BY current_balance_due DESC;
eli5Story: If a client paid an invoice with 3 partial payments, a raw join would duplicate the invoice 3 times and inflate counts. Pre-summing payments in a subquery keeps 1 row per invoice.
commonMistakes: Joining directly to an unaggregated payment table and summing invoice_amt, which artificially multiplies invoice totals by the number of payments!
learningOutcomes: Understand the 1-to-many join duplication trap and how right-side pre-aggregation guarantees accurate balances.

title: Fintech Bank Rec & Orphaned Disbursement Anti-Join Investigation #1
section: Section 8: Relational Joins & Financial Data Modeling
scenario: Detecting outstanding disbursements or idle accounts that exist in primary books but have zero records in verification feeds.
businessObjective: Write a LEFT ANTI-JOIN using WHERE right_table.key IS NULL to isolate unreconciled items.
schemaSnippet: `GeneralLedger_Fintech (check_id VARCHAR(32) PRIMARY KEY, recipient VARCHAR(64), amount_usd DECIMAL(12,2), issued_date DATE)` & `BankCleared_Fintech (check_num VARCHAR(32) PRIMARY KEY, cleared_date DATE)`
targetQuery:
SELECT gl.check_id, gl.recipient, gl.amount_usd, gl.issued_date
FROM GeneralLedger_Fintech gl
LEFT JOIN BankCleared_Fintech bk
  ON gl.check_id = bk.check_num
WHERE bk.check_num IS NULL
ORDER BY gl.issued_date ASC;
eli5Story: You have a checkbook and a bank statement. You LEFT JOIN them, and then filter WHERE the bank check is NULL. Only the checks you wrote that never cleared remain.
commonMistakes: Filtering on a nullable right column in WHERE instead of the primary key, risking false positives if that column naturally held NULLs.
learningOutcomes: Master the Left Anti-Join audit pattern for bank reconciliations and orphan detection.

title: Fintech Dual-Ledger Symmetric Reconciliation Audit #1
section: Section 8: Relational Joins & Financial Data Modeling
scenario: Performing a complete two-way audit between internal books and external settlement logs to find discrepancies on BOTH sides.
businessObjective: Use FULL OUTER JOIN to retain both internal-only and external-only records simultaneously.
schemaSnippet: `InternalLedger_Fintech (tx_id VARCHAR(32) PRIMARY KEY, internal_amount DECIMAL(12,2))` & `ExternalSettlement_Fintech (settle_id VARCHAR(32) PRIMARY KEY, external_amount DECIMAL(12,2))`
targetQuery:
SELECT COALESCE(a.tx_id, b.settle_id) AS unified_tx_id,
       a.internal_amount,
       b.external_amount,
       CASE
         WHEN a.tx_id IS NOT NULL AND b.settle_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'MATCHED_BOTH'
         WHEN a.tx_id IS NOT NULL AND b.settle_id IS NULL THEN 'INTERNAL_LEDGER_ONLY'
         ELSE 'EXTERNAL_BANK_ONLY'
       END AS audit_reconciliation_flag
FROM InternalLedger_Fintech a
FULL OUTER JOIN ExternalSettlement_Fintech b
  ON a.tx_id = b.settle_id
ORDER BY unified_tx_id ASC;
eli5Story: Like laying two bank records side by side. If both sides agree, they pair up. If internal recorded it but the bank didn't, you see it. If the bank took money but internal missed it, you see it too.
commonMistakes: Assuming FULL OUTER JOIN works natively in MySQL (it requires UNION of LEFT and RIGHT joins in MySQL, though supported natively in Postgres/Snowflake).
learningOutcomes: Understand symmetric dual-ledger audit visibility and handling multi-sided discrepancies.

title: Fintech Hierarchical Rollup & Period-over-Period Self Join #1
section: Section 8: Relational Joins & Financial Data Modeling
scenario: Resolving recursive parent-child reporting hierarchies or comparing current period metrics to prior period using dual aliasing of the same table.
businessObjective: Self join the entity table against itself to compute reporting trees or period-over-period growth variances.
schemaSnippet: `StaffRoster_Fintech (emp_id INT PRIMARY KEY, name VARCHAR(64), manager_id INT, salary DECIMAL(10,2))`
targetQuery:
SELECT e.emp_id, e.name AS employee_name,
       e.salary AS employee_salary,
       COALESCE(m.name, 'Board of Directors') AS manager_name,
       m.salary AS manager_salary,
       ROUND(e.salary / m.salary * 100, 1) AS salary_pct_of_manager
FROM StaffRoster_Fintech e
LEFT JOIN StaffRoster_Fintech m
  ON e.manager_id = m.emp_id
ORDER BY e.emp_id ASC;
eli5Story: The table has both employees and bosses in the same list. By giving the table two nicknames ('e' for employee and 'm' for manager), SQL links each employee to their own boss's row.
commonMistakes: Using an INNER JOIN which drops the CEO or top executive because their manager_id is NULL! Always use LEFT JOIN for managerial trees.
learningOutcomes: Master dual-aliasing recursive links and hierarchical relationship navigation.

title: Fintech Date Spine Calendar Scaffolding & Matrix Projection #1
section: Section 8: Relational Joins & Financial Data Modeling
scenario: Constructing a Cartesian date spine matrix pairing every active account with all 12 fiscal months so zero-activity periods are never omitted from charts.
businessObjective: Use CROSS JOIN to generate the Cartesian product of entities and reporting periods, left joining actual activity to guarantee clean reporting.
schemaSnippet: `ActiveAccounts_Fintech (account_id VARCHAR(32) PRIMARY KEY, account_name VARCHAR(64))` & `FiscalCalendar_Fintech (month_key VARCHAR(7) PRIMARY KEY)`
targetQuery:
SELECT a.account_id, a.account_name, c.month_key
FROM ActiveAccounts_Fintech a
CROSS JOIN FiscalCalendar_Fintech c
ORDER BY a.account_id ASC, c.month_key ASC;
eli5Story: If you want a chart of 12 months for 10 clients, you need 120 slots. A CROSS JOIN multiplies clients by months so even if a client bought nothing in May, May is still on the chart.
commonMistakes: Accidentally cross-joining two large transactional tables in production (100k x 100k = 10 Billion rows, causing memory failure).
learningOutcomes: Understand deliberate Cartesian products for date spines, sensitivity grids, and reporting templates.

scenario: Constructing a Cartesian date spine matrix pairing every active account with all 12 fiscal months so zero-activity periods are never omitted from charts.
businessObjective: Use CROSS JOIN to generate the Cartesian product of entities and reporting periods, left joining actual activity to guarantee clean reporting.
schemaSnippet: `ActiveAccounts_Logistics (account_id VARCHAR(32) PRIMARY KEY, account_name VARCHAR(64))` & `FiscalCalendar_Logistics (month_key VARCHAR(7) PRIMARY KEY)`
targetQuery:
SELECT a.account_id, a.account_name, c.month_key
FROM ActiveAccounts_Logistics a
CROSS JOIN FiscalCalendar_Logistics c
ORDER BY a.account_id ASC, c.month_key ASC;
eli5Story: If you want a chart of 12 months for 10 clients, you need 120 slots. A CROSS JOIN multiplies clients by months so even if a client bought nothing in May, May is still on the chart.
commonMistakes: Accidentally cross-joining two large transactional tables in production (100k x 100k = 10 Billion rows, causing memory failure).
learningOutcomes: Understand deliberate Cartesian products for date spines, sensitivity grids, and reporting templates.

scenario: Constructing a Cartesian date spine matrix pairing every active account with all 12 fiscal months so zero-activity periods are never omitted from charts.
businessObjective: Use CROSS JOIN to generate the Cartesian product of entities and reporting periods, left joining actual activity to guarantee clean reporting.
schemaSnippet: `ActiveAccounts_Platforms (account_id VARCHAR(32) PRIMARY KEY, account_name VARCHAR(64))` & `FiscalCalendar_Platforms (month_key VARCHAR(7) PRIMARY KEY)`
targetQuery:
SELECT a.account_id, a.account_name, c.month_key
FROM ActiveAccounts_Platforms a
CROSS JOIN FiscalCalendar_Platforms c
ORDER BY a.account_id ASC, c.month_key ASC;
eli5Story: If you want a chart of 12 months for 10 clients, you need 120 slots. A CROSS JOIN multiplies clients by months so even if a client bought nothing in May, May is still on the chart.
commonMistakes: Accidentally cross-joining two large transactional tables in production (100k x 100k = 10 Billion rows, causing memory failure).
learningOutcomes: Understand deliberate Cartesian products for date spines, sensitivity grids, and reporting templates.

title: Fintech Graduated Commission Tiers & Range Bracket Valuation #1
section: Section 8: Relational Joins & Financial Data Modeling
scenario: Mapping continuous sales figures or portfolio risk metrics into discrete compensation and tax brackets using BETWEEN min and max thresholds.
businessObjective: Perform a non-equi join on range condition BETWEEN to look up tiered payout schedules without hardcoding constants.
schemaSnippet: `SalesLog_Fintech (rep_id VARCHAR(32) PRIMARY KEY, rep_name VARCHAR(64), quarterly_volume DECIMAL(12,2))` & `TierLookup_Fintech (tier_name VARCHAR(32) PRIMARY KEY, min_vol DECIMAL(12,2), max_vol DECIMAL(12,2), commission_pct DECIMAL(5,2))`
targetQuery:
SELECT s.rep_name, s.quarterly_volume,
       t.tier_name, t.commission_pct,
       ROUND(s.quarterly_volume * (t.commission_pct / 100.0), 2) AS commission_payout_usd
FROM SalesLog_Fintech s
INNER JOIN TierLookup_Fintech t
  ON s.quarterly_volume BETWEEN t.min_vol AND t.max_vol
ORDER BY commission_payout_usd DESC;
eli5Story: Instead of checking if ID = ID, you check if sales fall between the minimum and maximum of a reward tier. A rep who sells $85,000 automatically lands in the $50k-$100k bracket.
commonMistakes: Creating overlapping tier brackets (e.g. 0-50k and 50k-100k) which causes a rep with exactly 50k to match twice and double their commission rows!
learningOutcomes: Master range-based join conditions, tiered compensation matrices, and eliminating hardcoded CASE WHENs.
